name: Character IP-Adapter SDXL (identity lock)
description: THE FOUR SEASONS character generation on SDXL. Locks face and art style to a base-ai reference image via IP-Adapter (golden rule #1: never rely on the text prompt alone for an existing character). SDXL only - ckpt 'speciosaAnime_v15.safetensors' for anime/illustration, 'RealVisXL_V5.0_fp16.safetensors' for the photoreal worldbuilding pass. Uses ip-adapter_sdxl_vit-h with the same clip_vision_h the sd15 pipeline uses. Sampler is pinned to euler_ancestral/karras. Prompt in danbooru tags: Speciosa is Pony-based, so lead with 'score_9, score_8_up, score_7_up, source_anime' and note that 'from above, kneeling, looking at viewer' beats a natural-language sentence. Only character_ref, prompt and filename_prefix have to be passed; everything else falls back to the defaults below. NOTE: IP-Adapter also carries over the reference's framing and lighting - a face-only reference biases the composition toward a portrait, and the SDXL IP-Adapter bites harder than the sd15 one: 0.85 collapses the shot into a face close-up and washes the palette out, 0.5 is the measured sweet spot where the prompt's framing and outfit survive. A face-only reference still forces a portrait crop at any weight - use a full-body reference, or char_ipadapter_controlnet_sdxl, when you need a full body. Native SDXL sizes are 832x1216 (portrait), 1024x1024, 1216x832 (landscape). ip_end is the fraction of sampling IP-Adapter stays active for. MEASURED, and not yet solved: this reference (kaede_face_front_base.jpg, a washed-out high-key face) transplants its palette and lighting onto the whole image. Alone that gives a desaturated portrait crop; combined with ControlNet it wrecks the colour outright - near-black at ip_end 1.0, magenta at 0.5, both with a yellow-green background cast. Shortening ip_end shifts the cast but does not remove it. With ip_weight 0 (ControlNet + prompt only) the same seed gives correct navy and clean values, so the cast is IP-Adapter's, not ControlNet's. Until this is calibrated, prefer ip_weight 0 for full-body/posed shots and treat identity locking as unresolved on the SDXL path. A LoRA slot sits between the checkpoint and everything downstream. lora_strength defaults to 0.0, which ComfyUI short-circuits before touching the file, so the slot costs nothing until used. For speed set lora_name 'Hyper-SDXL-8steps-CFG-lora.safetensors', lora_strength 1.0 and steps 8 - the CFG-preserving variant, so the usual cfg still applies. Do NOT use 'sdxl_lightning_8step_lora.safetensors' here: it forces cfg near 1.0, which collapses adherence to long outfit descriptions. MEASURED on the RTX 4070 Laptop (8GB VRAM / 15.6GB RAM): 30 steps takes 114s with a cold checkpoint and 72s warm; Hyper-SDXL 8 steps takes 96s on the run that loads the LoRA and 23s once it is cached - 3.1x faster than 30 steps, but only if nothing evicts it. The cost on this machine is loading, not sampling (checkpoint ~42s, LoRA ~72s), so batch every shot that shares a checkpoint and LoRA before switching, and POST /free between phases to reclaim RAM (worth ~3.6GB RAM and 2GB VRAM). Hyper's output is softer - fabric texture goes mushy and metal trim drifts - so use 8 steps to explore and 30 steps for the keeper.

defaults.negative_prompt: score_6, score_5, score_4, source_pony, source_furry, worst quality, low quality, bad anatomy, bad hands, bad feet, missing limbs, extra limbs, fused legs, cropped, out of frame, text, watermark, signature, jpeg artifacts, blurry
